learning_outcomes.text: Understand the operation and applications of hydraulic and pneumatic machines.
Dimension hydraulic machines subjected to general technical specifications.
Select pneumatic circuits for industrial applications.
Dimension fluid installations applying efficiency criteria in the design of the installation.
Knowledge in basic and technological subjects, enabling them to learn new methods and theories, and providing them with versatility to adapt to new situations.
Ability to solve problems with initiative, decision-making, creativity, critical reasoning, and to communicate and transmit knowledge, skills, and abilities in the field of Industrial Engineering.
Knowledge for carrying out measurements, calculations, valuations, appraisals, expert reports, studies, reports, work plans, and other similar tasks.
Applied knowledge of the fundamentals of fluid-mechanical systems and machines.

syllabus_topics: Definition and classification of hydraulic and pneumatic machines
Functional analysis of turbomachinery: series and parallel association
Cavitation and water hammer in a pump
Worldwide and Spanish utilization of hydraulic energy
Cavitation and water hammer in a turbine
Positive displacement hydraulic machines: piston pumps and rotostatic machines
assessment_rules: The general evaluation model is continuous assessment. No single assessment activity can individually exceed 60% of the global grade. The sum of non-re-evaluable activities cannot exceed 40% of the global grade. A minimum grade of 5 is required for each partial exam to be averaged with other activities, and a minimum of 4 is required in both the theoretical and problem-solving parts of each partial exam. Students who do not pass in the ordinary call, or do not attend, may present themselves to the extraordinary call only for the re-evaluable activities not passed. The final course grade must be 5 or higher.
